content: This document provides information about the medication golimumab, commonly sold under the brand name Simponi. It is important to note that this information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for every individual. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. Warning: Golimumab can suppress your immune system, reducing your body’s ability to fight infections. This suppression may lead to serious, potentially fatal infections, including fungal infections, bacterial infections, and tuberculosis (TB). Inform your doctor about your medical history, particularly any past, recent, or current infections. Additionally, let your doctor know if you have lived or traveled in areas where fungal infections like coccidioidomycosis or histoplasmosis are common, or if you have been in contact with someone who has TB. Your doctor will test you for TB before and during treatment with golimumab. There is also a rare risk of developing certain cancers, such as lymphoma or skin cancer, especially in children, teenagers, and young adults. This risk may be related to the medication or the underlying medical condition being treated. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of this treatment with your doctor. Uses: Golimumab is used to reduce pain and swelling associated with certain types of arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis. It works by blocking a protein in the immune system called tumor necrosis factor (TNF), which contributes to joint inflammation and damage. By reducing joint swelling, golimumab helps prevent further joint damage and preserves joint function. It is also used to treat ulcerative colitis, a chronic bowel condition. How to Use: Before starting golimumab, read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Review these materials each time you receive a refill. If you have any questions, consult your healthcare provider. Golimumab is administered as an injection under the skin, typically once a month, as directed by your doctor. The injection can be given in the thigh, abdomen, or upper arm. The dosage depends on your medical condition. For ulcerative colitis, your doctor may prescribe a different schedule or a higher dose at the beginning of treatment. Before injecting, remove the medication from the refrigerator at least 30 minutes in advance to allow it to reach room temperature. Do not warm the medication using other methods, such as a microwave or hot water. Avoid shaking the medication. Inspect the liquid for cloudiness, large particles, or discoloration before use. If you notice any of these, do not use the medication. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before each dose. Rotate injection sites to minimize skin injury. Avoid injecting into areas of skin that are sore, bruised, red, scaly, or hardened. To reduce bruising, do not rub the injection site after administering the medication. Use golimumab regularly to achieve the best results. Side Effects: Common side effects may include redness, itching, pain, or swelling at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to golimumab are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Precautions: Before using golimumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Golimumab may increase your risk of infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using golimumab before receiving any vaccinations or immunizations. During pregnancy, golimumab should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring: While using golimumab, your doctor may order regular lab tests, such as complete blood counts, liver function tests, and skin exams, to monitor your health. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. Storage: Store golimumab in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Keep the medication in its original carton to protect it from light. If necessary, the medication may be stored at room temperature. However, once stored at room temperature, do not return it to the refrigerator, and discard it after 30 days. Dispose of any unused portion after use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for another condition unless directed by your doctor. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
